newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French December bond futures surged to their fifth new contract high in seven sessions on Thursday before profit taking in the U.S. bond market knocked them off their new-found perch.
Analysts said the French market continued to be buoyed by domestic demand for bonds as the relatively high bid-to-cover ratio at Thursday's Treasury auction of government bonds demonstrated.
The December future climbed to 125.54, above the 125.50 peak reached by the September contract, early in the session and then remained range bound before slipping slightly before the close.
The Treasury sold 17.829 billion francs of OATs when the futures contract was near to its highs with an overall bid-to-cover ratio of 3.1.

As at last month's auction there was good demand for the TEC 10 variable rate bond. One primary dealer put in bids for five billion francs of the bond and received 2.65 billion out of the total 7.3 billion sold.

As expected the Bank of France left the intervention rate unchanged after its monetary policy counil metting on Thursday. Analysts said, however, they still expected call money to ease in the coming weeks.
The main focus on Friday will be the release of September U.S. non-farm payrolls which analysts polled by Reuters expected to show a 166,000 increase during the month.
"Some are expecting a very good figure tomorrow. It could well be a figure below 166,000," said one analyst.
Another analyst at a French bank in Paris said the hourly earnings component would the key figure in the release.
"The real economy numbers in the U.S. are not a threat, the key will be wages," he said.
The franc was slightly weaker late on Thursday at 3.3845 compared with 3.3830 on Wednesday.
